## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammadhajajātaka* (Ja 220) is a narrative belonging to the Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. In the edition of the *Jātaka* commentary by V. Fausböll, the text concludes as the tenth story (*dasamaṁ*) of its vagga [Fausböll 1879]. 

According to its background narrative, the Buddha delivered the story while residing at the Bamboo Grove near Rājagaha concerning attempts by Devadatta to assassinate him [SuttaCentral]. Assuring the saṅgha that Devadatta had previously tried to kill him without succeeding in frightening him, the Buddha recounted the narrative of their past lives [SuttaCentral]. Four modern translations across four languages are registered for the text on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Curated records and automated analyses indicate an absence of identified parallels: SuttaCentral records no external or canonical parallels for Ja 220 [SuttaCentral], and DharmaNexus reports no internal Pali reuse matches or cross-language alignments meeting its threshold score [DharmaNexus].
